disagreements.topic: 2027 normalized EPS growth (agent_3 +20% haircut vs consensus +29%)
disagreements.positions: All five now accept the round-1 correction (FY26 normalized $8.15 -> FY27 $10.48). Agents 1, 2, 4, 5 use consensus with ~+20% into FY28 (NTM EPS $11.8-12.05). agent_3 keeps a core FY27 EPS of $9.80 (+20%) on depreciation lag and capex at 102% of OCF, which is the main reason its fair value ($240) and P(>=247) (0.53) sit below the group ($263-271, 0.55-0.59).
disagreements.resolution: The haircut is a legitimate skeptic view, but the evidence runs against it for now. FY27 consensus has been revised up from $9.96 to $10.48 over 90 days (8 up vs 1 down in 30 days). Amazon's own Q3-26 guide is operating income of $22.5-26.5B versus $17.4B in Q3-25, i.e. +29-52% even as sales growth is guided to only +9-12% because Prime Day moved into June. D&A growth (~67% at AWS) is real, but it is already in the guide. I pull a small part of agent_3's gap toward the group (about +0.004 in the middle strikes), not all of it: capex > OCF and the D&A lag are real, and the trend could turn.
disagreements.evidence: Amazon Q2-26 8-K Ex.99.1 (Q3 guidance); stockanalysis.com consensus (FY26 $8.15, FY27 $10.48, 59 analysts); 24/7 Wall St revision data (secondary)

disagreements.topic: Rate backdrop: did the Fed actually hike?
disagreements.positions: agent_5 cut its multiple and ladder citing a 'Sep 16 hike' and 45-70% odds of another on Oct 28. Agents 1, 2 and 4 mention hike odds only, and agent_3 mentions them alongside CDS widening.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed. On Sep 16, 2026 the FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% by a 12-0 vote, its first hike since 2023. The median dot shows one more hike in 2026. agent_5's trim to 23x is justified, and the others' 23-23.5x already reflects it. A second hike is largely priced, so this supports holding the multiple, not a further cut.
disagreements.evidence: CNBC 2026-09-16 'Fed rate decision September 2026: Rates rise to 3.75%-4%'; Federal Reserve implementation note 2026-09-16

disagreements.topic: AI capacity glut vs firm pricing (AWS bear case)
disagreements.positions: The bear scenarios of agents 2, 3 and 4 assume GPU pricing rolls over or AI demand digests. agent_4's new alt data says rental prices are firming.
disagreements.resolution: Verified. The getdeploying H100 rental index median is $3.42/hr, +15% y/y and +3.2% over 4 weeks (week of Sep 28, 2026). This is independent of company commentary and argues against a near-term glut. It does not settle 2027 demand, so the ~22-25% bear weights stay.

disagreements.topic: Q3 comps: Prime Day in June
disagreements.positions: Only agent_4 (Tinuiti) flags that Prime Day moved into Q2, which flattered the Q2 retail/ads run-rate. Others extrapolate Q2's +20% sales growth.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed. Prime Day 2026 ran June 23-26 (Amazon), and the Q3 guide of +9-12% sales growth reflects the shift. The Q3 print (expected Oct 29, after the close) will show a headline deceleration that is calendar-driven. This matters for how the print is read, not for fair value. Agents deriving retail run-rates from Q2 should normalize them.
disagreements.evidence: aboutamazon.com 'Prime Day 2026: Amazon's 4-day deal event starts June 23'; Q2-26 8-K Ex.99.1 guidance

disagreements.topic: Anthropic IPO timing inside the 1-month window
disagreements.positions: agent_5: Polymarket 4.5% by Oct 31, despite press talk of an October listing. Others: a 'small chance of a public S-1'.
disagreements.resolution: Consistent. Press reports say Anthropic targets an October Nasdaq listing, but no public S-1 had been filed by Sep 30, and a public filing must precede the roadshow by at least 15 days. A listing by Oct 29 is therefore unlikely. A public S-1 in the window is plausible and would be two-sided news for the $190.4B mark. No change to the 1-month center.
disagreements.evidence: Fortune/NPR 2026-06-01 on the confidential S-1; press reports of an October target (secondary); Polymarket via agent_5

disagreements.positions: All five: Thu Oct 29 after the close (estimated)
disagreements.resolution: Still not confirmed by Amazon as of Sep 30; no Q3 webcast notice has been posted (the Q2 notice came 14 days before the print). Keep slightly wide 1-month tails.

one_month_reasoning: No company event is confirmed in the window: Q3 results are expected Thu Oct 29 after the close, so the scored close is most likely pre-print. The Oct 28 FOMC comes after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%, with a second hike largely priced. Other in-window items are Prime Big Deal Days (Oct 6-7), late-October Microsoft/Alphabet/Meta cloud and capex read-through, and a possible public Anthropic S-1 (a listing by Oct 29 is unlikely). The five revised 1-month ladders agree closely and already widen the tails for these, so I keep their mean.
confidence_reason: Round 2 converged: fair values are $240-271 and P(>=247) is 0.53-0.59, with the factual disputes of round 1 resolved in the revisions. My new checks confirm the Sep 16 Fed hike (supporting agent_5's trim), firm GPU rental pricing, and a Q3 operating-income guide and upward EPS revisions that argue against agent_3's EPS haircut. These justify only a small nudge (about +0.004 in the middle strikes), not a replacement of the mean.
thesis_break_reason: All five agents again land on $185, unchanged from round 1. That is ~25% below spot, below the ~$196 52-week low, and ~17.5x FY27 consensus EPS of $10.48, which is growing ~29%. Getting there needs AWS growth breaking toward the low 20s, a backlog renegotiation, or an Anthropic mark reversal combined with credit stress. That is more than 34%-vol noise.

Normalized EPS path: FY26 $8.15 -> FY27 $10.48 (+29%, revised up from $9.96 in 90 days); the Q3 OI guide of $22.5-26.5B vs $17.4B supports delivery
Rates: the Fed hiked on Sep 16, 2026 to 3.75-4.00% and signals one more; Amazon's debt is ~$154B pro forma, which caps the multiple at ~23x forward

fair_value.reason: The revised agents' mean is $261.4 ($240-271) after all five adopted the corrected inputs (Anthropic $190.4B carrying / ~$160B after tax, net debt ~$42B incl. Globalstar, normalized EPS +29%). I give agent_3's $9.80 core EPS a partial weight only, because consensus is being revised up and the Q3 OI guide is strong. P/E: ~$12.0 NTM EPS x 23x = $276. SOTP ~$250. A 60/40 blend of the two gives ~$270. I shade it to $264 for the confirmed hiking cycle and capex > OCF (round 1: $265).

summary: Round 2 converged: the five revised fair values span $240-271 (mean $261), P(>=$247) is 0.53-0.59, and all keep the $185 thesis break. My checks confirm the Sep 16 Fed hike (rates now cap the multiple at ~23x) and firm GPU rental pricing. EPS revisions and the Q3 operating-income guide cut against the skeptic's EPS haircut, so I nudge the middle of the ladder up slightly (P(>=247) 0.570 vs 0.566 mean), with fair value at $264. Watch the Oct 28 FOMC and the Q3 print (expected Oct 29, after the close), where the sales slowdown from the Prime Day timing shift could be misread.

sizing.entry: 2 tranches over ~5 weeks: half now, half after the Oct 28 FOMC and the Q3 print (expected Oct 29, after the close)
sizing.overlap: None; the book is all cash. AMZN carries broad Nasdaq and AI-capex beta that later tech buys would share.
sizing.reason: Round 2 leaves a modest, well-agreed edge (median ~+5-7%, P(>=spot) ~0.57) on a very liquid mega-cap, so liquidity is no constraint. Two events land within a month: an FOMC in an active hiking cycle, and a Q3 print whose headline sales will look weak from the Prime Day shift. Cap the first position at ~12% and stage the entry around them.
sizing.confidence_source: confidence pass 2026-10-01 (beats S&P 500 12M Sharpe): The edge rests on ~29% normalized EPS growth, AWS +37% with a $496B backlog and a ~$264 fair value, but the median is only ~+5-7% while realized vol (~30%+) is about twice SPY's, so it needs a clearly larger return to win on Sharpe. Main risks are capex above operating cash flow (negative TTM FCF) with depreciation ramping, a hiking Fed capping the ~23x multiple, and the Oct 29 print.
